statements.impact_statement: Debian lists this use-after-free in xmlParseInternalSubset as present in trixie's libxml2 (2.9.14 based; Debian security tracker, CVE-2026-6653) and marks it no-dsa. PostgreSQL parses a document's internal DTD subset whenever text is cast to xml or passed to XMLPARSE, so a session can reach it. libxml2 is linked into the PostgreSQL server, and every database session can reach it without any privilege, through a cast to xml, XMLPARSE, XMLSERIALIZE, xpath() and XMLTABLE. FerroEHR's server sends none of these (its schemas have no xml column and it parses openEHR XML in Rust), so the exposure is a database login used outside FerroEHR: an administrator's session, a reporting tool, or a stolen credential. A backend that crashes makes the postmaster restart every session.
statements.action_statement: Grant database logins only to the FerroEHR roles and to administrators, and keep the database port reachable only from the FerroEHR server and administration hosts (the chart's NetworkPolicy and the compose network do this). Give any other tool that needs SQL access its own role and treat it as able to stop the database. The fix arrives with Debian's next libxml2 update for trixie, which the image's security-upgrade layer installs on the first release build after Debian publishes it.

The overflow is in the xmlcatalog command-line utility's --shell mode. xmlcatalog ships in libxml2-utils, which this image does not install; the libxml2 library package contains no copy of the utility.
The double free is in libxml2's Python bindings (the SAX attributeDecl callback of the Python module). The image installs no Python and no python3-libxml2 package, so the bindings are not present.

The NULL dereference is in XML catalog parsing. libxml2 reads catalogs only from its default external-entity loader; PostgreSQL replaces that loader with xmlPgEntityLoader, which returns an empty string for every external resource (src/backend/utils/adt/xml.c, PostgreSQL 18.6), so no catalog is ever opened. The image has no /etc/xml catalog either.

The overflow is in xmlSnprintfElements, which libxml2 calls only while validating an element against a DTD content model. PostgreSQL parses with XML_PARSE_NOENT, XML_PARSE_DTDATTR and XML_PARSE_NOBLANKS (src/backend/utils/adt/xml.c, PostgreSQL 18.6): it applies DTD attribute defaults but never requests validation (no XML_PARSE_DTDVALID, no xmlValidate* call), so the function is not reached.

The overflow is in libxml2's XPointer evaluator (xmlXPtrEval). PostgreSQL's xpath(), xpath_exists() and XMLTABLE evaluate XPath 1.0 through xmlXPathCompile and xmlXPathCompiledEval on a plain XPath context (src/backend/utils/adt/xml.c, PostgreSQL 18.6) and never create an XPointer context, and XInclude, the other caller, is never run (see CVE-2026-86144).

The flaw is in XInclude processing (xmlXIncludeProcess, xmlXIncludeProcessTree). PostgreSQL never calls either function and does not pass XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE (src/backend/utils/adt/xml.c, PostgreSQL 18.6). The only other XInclude user in the image is libxslt in the contrib xml2 module, an untrusted extension that is not created in any database and that only a superuser could create.

The CPU and memory exhaustion needs a crafted pattern passed to glibc glob(). The postgres binary does not import glob; in the server process the only caller is libgssapi_krb5, which globs its own fixed mechanism-configuration path (/etc/gss/mech.d). bash, which runs the entrypoint, matches patterns with its own code. No pattern an attacker supplies reaches glob().

The uncontrolled recursion needs a crafted pattern passed to glibc regcomp and regexec. PostgreSQL has its own regular-expression engine (src/backend/regex) and the postgres binary imports neither function; in the server process only libkrb5 calls them, for auth_to_local rules in the root-owned krb5.conf, which the image does not configure. No pattern an attacker supplies reaches glibc's matcher.

glibc upstream (sourceware bug 22850) and Debian do not treat this as a vulnerability: it describes a way to defeat the stack protector after an attacker already holds a stack buffer overflow in the process. It is not a fault an input can trigger; an attacker who has such an overflow in this image's processes is answered by that overflow's own statement or fix.

The issue needs ldd to be run on an attacker-supplied ELF file. Nothing in this image runs ldd: the entrypoint, initdb, psql and the server never invoke it, and no deployment path gives anyone an interactive shell in the container.

glibc upstream (sourceware bug 22852) and Debian do not treat this as a vulnerability: the reuse of cached thread stacks and heaps can make addresses easier to guess, which matters only to an attacker who already holds a memory-corruption primitive in the process. No input to this image triggers it on its own.

glibc upstream (sourceware bug 22853) and Debian do not treat this as a vulnerability; the glibc position is that an ASLR bypass is not a vulnerability by itself. Guessing a pthread heap address helps only an attacker who already holds a memory-corruption primitive, and the PostgreSQL server is a multi-process server that creates few threads.

The overflow is in the aligned operator new path that rounds the size before calling C11 aligned_alloc. libstdc++ prefers posix_memalign where it exists (libsupc++/new_opa.cc, GCC 14.2.0), and on GNU/Linux it does: the shipped libstdc++.so.6 imports posix_memalign and not aligned_alloc, and the upstream fix states that posix_memalign targets are not affected.

The use-after-free is in erase_if of the policy-based binary heap, a header-only template (include/ext/pb_ds/detail/binary_heap_/erase_fn_imps.hpp, per the GCC fix for PR127656). It is compiled into a program only when that program uses __gnu_pbds; libstdc++.so.6 does not contain it, and the C++ code in this image (ICU and LLVM) does not use the policy-based data structures.

The traversal needs an attacker who sets the LANGUAGE environment variable of a process that translates messages with gettext, and a crafted .mo file that process can read (GLIBC-SA-2026-0025). PostgreSQL translates its messages and runs with lc_messages taken from the image's LANG (en_US.utf8), so the server would honour LANGUAGE. Every process in the image (the entrypoint's bash, gosu, initdb, psql, the postmaster and each backend) inherits its environment from the container, which only the operator's compose file, chart or runtime sets; the image sets no LANGUAGE. No connection, protocol message, setting or SQL function available to the ferroehr role sets a variable in a server process's environment: the variables PostgreSQL writes itself are the LC_* names, from values setlocale has accepted, and PGLOCALEDIR and PGSYSCONFDIR, from its install paths. A role that could set one (a superuser through an untrusted procedural language) already runs code as the postgres user, so it crosses no trust boundary.

The leak is in code that LLVM generates for the Armv8-M Cortex-M Security Extensions (CMSE). libLLVM is loaded here only by PostgreSQL's JIT provider (llvmjit.so), which compiles for the host CPU, an x86-64 or Armv8-A processor; it never targets an M-profile core, so the CMSE code path is never taken.

libLLVM is loaded only by PostgreSQL's JIT provider, llvmjit.so. The IR it compiles is built by PostgreSQL from query plans, and the only bitcode it reads is the image's own root-owned llvmjit_types.bc and the inlining bitcode under /usr/lib/postgresql/18/lib/bitcode; no LLVM command-line tool is installed. No IR or bitcode an attacker writes reaches LLVM's readers. The report is a crash in StringMap::insert while an LLVM command-line tool reads crafted IR; Debian records it as a crash in a CLI tool with no security impact (Debian security tracker, CVE-2026-13573).

Debian ties this note to CVE-2016-7543: bash started with a real user id different from its effective one does not drop privileges to the real user. bash runs here only as the entrypoint, first as root and then through gosu, a setpriv wrapper that sets the real and effective ids to the same postgres user, so bash never starts with differing ids.
Debian's note concerns the no-root option of the Debian expert installer. No installer code is in this image; sysvinit-utils provides only utilities the entrypoint does not use.

The heap overflow is in the client side of Cyrus SASL's DIGEST-MD5 mechanism, reached when a SASL client authenticates to a hostile server. The image carries libsasl2 only as a dependency of libldap. PostgreSQL's LDAP authentication binds with ldap_simple_bind_s (src/backend/libpq/auth.c) and never starts a SASL bind, and libpq's SCRAM is its own implementation, so no process in the image runs the DIGEST-MD5 client.

The NULL dereference is in the Kerberos KDC (get_pac_princ_with_realm, krb5kdc's S4U2Proxy handling). The image carries the krb5 client libraries PostgreSQL links (libkrb5-3, libgssapi-krb5-2, libk5crypto3, libkrb5support0) and no KDC: the krb5-kdc package is not installed, so the vulnerable code is not in the image.

The NULL dereference is in libkrb5's make_cred_list (rd_cred.c), reached through gss_accept_sec_context when an authenticated Kerberos client forwards mismatched credentials. PostgreSQL accepts a GSSAPI context only for gss or hostgssenc entries in pg_hba.conf with a server keytab (krb_server_keyfile). The configuration FerroEHR ships has neither, but an operator's configuration can, so the image is affected. The crash ends the one backend that accepted the context.
statements.action_statement: Do not configure GSSAPI authentication or GSS encryption (gss or hostgssenc in pg_hba.conf with krb_server_keyfile) on the database until Debian ships the fix; FerroEHR connects with password (SCRAM) authentication and needs neither. Debian marks the fix no-dsa for trixie; the image's security-upgrade layer installs it on the first release build after Debian publishes it.

statements.impact_statement: Debian security tracker, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-114690: an out-of-bounds access in the libstdc++ parallel search implementation, reached by crafted search data in an application compiled with parallel mode (trixie: no DSA, minor issue). The GCC fix, commit c1f32b67510f, changes only include/parallel/search.h, a header template compiled into a program built with _GLIBCXX_PARALLEL and OpenMP. libstdc++.so.6 does not contain it: its only __gnu_parallel exports are _Settings::get and _Settings::set (nm -D on the rc8 images). No program in this image is built in parallel mode: libgomp, the OpenMP runtime parallel mode requires, is not installed, and no ELF object in the image lists it in DT_NEEDED (readelf over every executable and shared object of the rc8 image). PostgreSQL itself is C and does not link libstdc++.so.6.

Debian security tracker, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-114691: an integer wrap in the std::vector<bool> constructors when a caller passes an excessively large element count, leaving the container inconsistent and leading to out-of-bounds access (trixie: no DSA, minor issue). The GCC fix, commit 2fd8866591b5, changes only include/bits/stl_bvector.h, adding a check that the count does not exceed max_size(); the constructors are header templates compiled into the program that calls them. libstdc++.so.6 does not contain them: it exports no std::vector<bool> symbol (nm -D on the rc8 images). PostgreSQL itself is C and does not link libstdc++.so.6. The C++ libraries it loads, ICU for collations and LLVM through llvmjit.so for JIT compilation, export no std::vector<bool> instantiation; a copy inlined into them belongs to libicu76 or libllvm19, not to the packages this finding names. The wrap needs a count above max_size(), which no count of objects held in memory can reach, only a negative value or an unchecked external integer converted to size_t.

The ferroehr-postgres image is the official postgres:18 image on Debian trixie with the build-time GnuPG toolchain purged and gosu replaced by a POSIX-sh wrapper; its processes are the PostgreSQL server and its children, started by the upstream docker-entrypoint.sh. The server is built with OpenSSL and maps libssl.so.3 and libcrypto.so.3 from libssl3t64 for TLS on client connections (the ssl settings an operator enables), for SCRAM-SHA-256 and its tls-server-end-point channel binding (a hash of the server certificate), and for its own hashing and random numbers. The image also carries the openssl command-line program and the legacy provider (openssl-provider-legacy), which no process of the image runs or loads: the entrypoint and the server never execute openssl, and the legacy provider is loaded only when an OpenSSL configuration names it, which neither the image nor FerroEHR does. The flaw is in the QUIC stack of OpenSSL 3.5.7 (libssl): its automated peer detection reads the peer address into a buffer too short for it (OpenSSL security advisory of 2026-11-10). PostgreSQL speaks TLS over TCP through the SSL_CTX and SSL API on a stream socket and never creates a QUIC connection, so the QUIC code is not reached. Debian has no fix for trixie, and the statement goes when the image carries one.

PostgreSQL has its own regular-expression engine (src/backend/regex): the postgres binary and every module under /usr/lib/postgresql/18/lib import neither regcomp nor regexec (objdump -T on the :main image of 2026-11-13, both architectures). Of the libraries the PostgreSQL server and its modules load, two import iconv_open: libxml2 and libstdc++ (objdump -T over every ELF file of the :main image of 2026-11-25 (sha256:be3e3d75), 992 on amd64 and 991 on arm64); the other importers (bash, cmp, diff, diff3, iconv, printf, sdiff, tar, libapt-pkg, libidn2 and libunistring) run only in programs an operator starts by hand. libxml2 opens the converters for an encoding name as iconv_open("UTF-8", name) to decode and iconv_open(name, "UTF-8") to encode, so the CP949 decoder only ever runs towards the fixed destination UTF-8, and glibc reads //IGNORE from the destination name alone. FerroEHR has not shown that no PostgreSQL XML function hands libxml2 the encoding a document declares, so any database session that may call those functions is taken to reach the decoder: a cast to xml, XMLPARSE, xpath() and XMLTABLE, and xslt_process where the xml2 extension is installed. FerroEHR's server sends none of these (its schemas have no xml column and it parses openEHR XML in Rust), so the exposure is a database login used outside FerroEHR: an administrator's session, a reporting tool, or a stolen credential. statements.action_statement: Grant database logins only to the FerroEHR roles and to administrators, and keep the database port reachable only from the FerroEHR server and administration hosts (the chart's NetworkPolicy and the compose network do this). Give any other tool that needs SQL access its own role and treat it as able to stop the database. The fix arrives with Debian's next glibc update for trixie, which the image's security-upgrade layer installs on the first release build after Debian publishes it.
